requiredFindings.title: The mixed-read retry is a second monitor read
requiredFindings.failureScenario: FreshnessMonitor::read latches the gate on the first callback error. Item 5 repeats the observation once within the same tick when the reopened state.v1 identity differs, and treats only a second mixed view as fail-stop. A publication that renames state.v1 during the callback returns that mismatch, the monitor latches, and the operation fail-stops on a lawful atomic replacement. Both attempts have to run inside the one callback. The callback returns a coherent admitted view when the second attempt matches, and it returns the latching error only for a still-mixed second view, an unreadable record, a failed authentication, or a floor or rollback rejection.

requiredFindings.title: A dropped lease is reported as a changed file
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Item 8 sends an owner, lease, or endpoint change to the custody or busy row with subject required-files-changed. That subject is the custody row for a required file that changed. The lease guard also fails when the admitted fd is unchanged and the lock is no longer held. That case is S7 PROJECT.BUSY, operational-failed, exit 4, LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT. An implementer who follows the parenthetical reports CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED subject required-files-changed for a dropped lock. A replaced lease file, owner, or endpoint keeps the custody row. A lock that is no longer held keeps the busy row.

scope: Law X4 r2. Codex RF-1, RF-2, RF-4, and RF-5 are closed. Splitting out X4T is sound. Drift matches observe_revocation. The one-retry bound is sound, and the retry is specified as another observation after FreshnessMonitor latches on the first mismatch. A dropped lease is reported as required-files-changed. No product cargo.
